title: AETHER Phase 5 — SNAP real-graph benchmark

protocol.method_order: rotated deterministically by seed and repeat
protocol.warmup: small graph and query/update calls before each measured construction
protocol.same_workload: identical SHA-256 of deterministic event/query stream per dataset, mode, seed and repeat; answers checked against a separate set-based BFS replay
protocol.queries: balanced positive/negative sampling; positives are generated by following existing directed edges, negatives originate from sink nodes when available and are verified by independent BFS
protocol.dynamic_workload: two rounds of deterministic absent-edge insertions and present-edge removals, with query windows before and after changes
protocol.timing: construction, update, query, total workload, process CPU, worker startup end-to-end excluding oracle, and parsing/preparation are separate
protocol.percentiles: per-query p50/p95/p99 for single-call methods; batch-call p50/p95/p99 and mean time per pair for FFI batch; these distributions are not interchangeable
protocol.ffi_cost_decomposition: diagnostic after the main workload: Python pair packing, output-buffer and pointer setup, raw Rust batch call, zero-hop batch floor, memoryview creation, and bytes materialization are reported separately. The zero-hop call still scans and validates pairs; real-minus-zero-hop is only an estimate of added graph processing, not pure transfer time.
protocol.rss: RSS sampled around graph construction; process peak is platform-dependent and null where no trustworthy standard-library measure is available
protocol.memory: retained graph value is an implementation-specific estimate; it is not interchangeable with RSS
protocol.new_capabilities: shortest-path reconstruction and two-hop neighborhood are timed separately and verified against independent BFS on the final state

methods.python_sets: Python set adjacency with DFS and per-query visited set
methods.python_compact: Python array('I') adjacency with reusable epoch marks
methods.python_csr: immutable Python CSR snapshot; static workloads only
methods.rust_ffi_single: Rust mutable rows with one FFI call per query/update
methods.rust_ffi_batch: same Rust mutable rows with one FFI call per query/update group and caller-reused output buffer
methods.feature_policy: pre-run rule uses node/edge counts, density, estimated memory, expected update/query ratio and budget; it does not learn these evaluation graphs
methods.online_controller: existing EMA controller selects between exact Python set-visited and epoch-mark DFS based on observed query timings; its decision cost is included
methods.best_fixed: reported as the lowest observed median among applicable fixed methods, not as an additional implementation

limitations: Different query seeds over one public graph do not constitute independent datasets.
SNAP pages consulted do not state dataset-specific licenses for the selected datasets; the unknown status is recorded and the software SNAP BSD license is not attributed to the data.
BFS-based query generation intentionally balances positive and negative answers; it is not an application production trace.
The feature policy is a simple fixed heuristic, not a trained predictor; its results do not establish generalization beyond the evaluated graphs.
The online controller calibrates on a training query window and is measured on a later window, but graph-family diversity remains limited.
No joules or FLOPs are reported; CPU time is not converted to energy.
Windows is not available in the execution environment; no Windows result is claimed.
